title: Making Latent Evolution Explicit: Operator-Structured Transitions for World Action Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.27259v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) augment robot policies by predicting how task-relevant scene states may evolve under interaction. Recent WAMs increasingly perform such prediction in latent representation spaces, avoiding full appearance-level generation while preserving control-relevant information. Yet latent transitions are commonly realized with Transformer-based predictors whose inductive structure is centered on token interaction rather than temporal evolution. We study transition realization as an architectural choice distinct from predictive representation and prediction-policy coupling. We introduce the Latent Evolution Operator Network (LEON), which models latent evolution in a learned observable space through context-modulated operator-based propagation and additive forcing. translated_title: 将潜在演化显式化：面向世界动作模型的算子结构化转换
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.27259v1 公告类型：新  摘要：世界动作模型（WAMs）通过预测任务相关场景状态在交互下可能如何演化来增强机器人策略。近年来，WAMs越来越多地在潜在表示空间中进行此类预测，避免了完整外观级生成，同时保留了控制相关信息。然而，潜在转换通常通过基于Transformer的预测器实现，其归纳结构侧重于标记交互而非时间演化。我们将转换实现视为一种架构选择，区别于预测表示和预测-策略耦合。我们引入了潜在演化算子网络（LEON），该网络通过上下文调制的基于算子的传播和加性强迫，在学习的可观测空间中建模潜在演化。基于受控Koopman生成器的演化视角，LEON将上下文相关的转换变化组织在共享的演化算子结构周围。
tldr: 本文提出LEON模型，通过算子结构化转换显式建模潜在演化，替代Transformer的标记交互方式，以提升世界动作模型在时间演化预测上的效果。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces LEON, which models latent evolution explicitly via operator-structured transitions, replacing Transformer's token interaction to improve temporal evolution prediction in World Action Models.
